source: User-provided IT 105 Discrete Structures 1 PPT/PPTM modules
readMethod: Read-only OOXML text and Office Math extraction using both transitional and strict namespace local names. No VBA executed and original documents unchanged. Serialized actual scene catalog references were exported by Unity for source-template inspection.

topics.name: Propositional Logic
stages: Identify a connective from three truth-value observations
topics.alignment: The same conjunction, inclusive disjunction, exclusive OR, implication and biconditional semantics. Fantasy scenarios and observation logs are game adaptations, not slide quotations.

topics.name: Truth Table
topics.alignment: Four TT/TF/FT/FF output rows combine only the taught connectives and negation. New compound expressions apply the module rules; the separate formula parser checks all authored 24 formulas.

topics.name: Rules of Inference
topics.alignment: Each stage has premise-word assembly followed by rule identification. Compound premise substitutions retain valid module rules. Other taught rules/equivalences are distractor choices, not unrelated material.

topics.name: Formal vs Informal Proofs
topics.alignment: Explicit premises, valid justifications and natural-language explanations implement the module distinction. Parity/divisibility examples and formalization tasks are applications of these skills.

topics.name: Direct and Indirect Proofs
stages: Identify the supplied strategy and arrange a direct proof
Identify and arrange one of the three strategies
topics.alignment: Uses only direct, contrapositive and contradiction proof strategies taught by the module. Integer parity/divisibility and no-extremum rational examples are valid variations of the same proof techniques; not every theorem appears verbatim on the slides.

topics.name: Mathematical Induction
topics.alignment: Applies the base/hypothesis/step/conclusion structure to finite arithmetic series. Affine-term series are algebraic variations of the module arithmetic-series proof, not a new induction technique.

topics.name: Sets
stages: A, B, intersection and differences: 2 problems
Complement in an explicit universe: 2 problems
topics.alignment: Roster and set-builder notation, membership, Venn regions, set difference and complement stay within the module. Numeric values and physical delivery are adaptations. Five challenges of two problems are preserved.

topics.name: Functions and Relations
stages: Build a relation from ordered-pair conditions
Classify a relation as a function
topics.alignment: Ordered pairs, domain/codomain/range, exactly one output per input, one-to-one, onto and bijection follow the module. Explicit finite mappings and unused codomain values are valid exercises of the taught definitions.

topics.name: Graphs
stages: Inspect vertices/edges while tracing a simple path
topics.alignment: Uses only vertices, edges, direction, degree, path and cycle. Walking routes is the physical adaptation. No shortest-path algorithm, Euler/Hamilton theorem or graph coloring is required.

topics.name: Trees
stages: Depth or height by edge count
Remove edges to obtain a spanning tree
topics.alignment: Root, parent/child, depth, height and spanning-tree properties follow the module. Any valid spanning tree is accepted. No search-tree ordering, AVL balancing or traversal algorithm is required.

correctionsMade: T4 missing-justification round now removes unrelated copied Solo proof steps; only the newly generated argument appears.
T3 source reference now explicitly includes all relevant Week 3 rules and Week 4 equivalence distractors; T4 source reference includes both inference weeks.
moduleErrataPreservedAsCorrectMath: Midterm Weeks 8-9 slides 13-15 mix odd-number summands with the arithmetic-series formula. Gameplay uses the correct sum of affine terms; the sum of the first n odd numbers is n squared.
Midterm Week 7 slide 15 labels a divisibility claim but gives a smallest-positive-number argument. Gameplay proof statements and their steps remain matched.
Final Weeks 17-18 slide 4 mixes undirected trees and rooted directed orientations. Gameplay distinguishes them.
Final Weeks 17-18 slide 12 gives a binary-tree level bound as a general tree property. Gameplay does not use it as a universal tree rule.

templateInspection.formalProofScrollPool: All ten variants of the actual four-scroll classification family and ten five-step ordering variants read. Missing-rule and final formalization builders inspected separately.
templateInspection.proofMethods: All 40 selectable direct, contrapositive, contradiction and choose-and-arrange templates read.
templateInspection.graph: All selectable saved graph variants inspected; directed cycle adaptation follows arrows and simple-cycle uniqueness.
templateInspection.tree: Current multiplayer builder uses the actual seven-node source, then explicit build/repair/depth/height/spanning variations.
templateInspection.inference: Every selected structural inference checked against all 16 valuations by Unity verification entrypoint.
templateInspection.induction: Every generated arithmetic family follows sum(a*i+b)=n(a*n+a+2*b)/2 with base and next-term identities.

limits: Concept and mathematical-content alignment, not a claim that every sentence or theorem is copied verbatim from a slide. Image-only slide diagrams and every visual PowerPoint layout were not rendered individually. Medium/hard difficulty labels require student playtesting.
